s.note: the grits cross-examination, nobody can cook them that fast
s.how: Bring 500ml milk and 500ml water to the boil with 1 tsp salt. Whisk in 150g stone-ground grits or polenta, then stir over low heat for 25 minutes until creamy. Finish with 40g butter and 80g grated sharp cheddar. Not five minutes, whatever anyone says.

Slice 3 green tomatoes 1cm thick, salt and leave 10 minutes, then pat dry. Dip in 150ml buttermilk, then 120g fine cornmeal seasoned with salt and pepper, and shallow-fry at 180C for 2 minutes a side. Mix 100g mayonnaise, 1 tsp mustard, 1 tbsp chopped capers and a dash of hot sauce for the remoulade.

m.note: the corner store where the whole mess started
m.how: Pound 4 minute steaks, about 600g, very thin. Dredge in seasoned flour, dip in 200ml buttermilk, then flour again, and shallow-fry 3 minutes a side until crisp. Pour off most of the oil, stir 2 tbsp flour into the pan, whisk in 400ml milk and simmer thick with lots of black pepper. Serve over 800g mashed potato.

w.note: Wazoo, Alabama, ticking clock and all
w.how: Toss 750g blackberries with 100g sugar and 1 tbsp cornflour in a dish. Rub 80g butter into 200g self-raising flour and 50g sugar, add 150ml milk and drop spoonfuls on top. Bake at 190C for 35 minutes and serve with 300ml cream.

d.note: Southern style in Wazoo, Alabama, so sweet your teeth hurt
d.how: Simmer 2 sliced ripe peaches with 120g caster sugar and 150ml water for 10 minutes, mash lightly and strain, keeping the syrup. Steep 6 black tea bags in 1 litre just-boiled water for 5 minutes and remove. Stir in the peach syrup and juice of half a lemon, then chill for 2 hours. Serve over ice with fresh peach slices and mint.
